4. Place the title 'Data Overfit and Underfit' centered at the top of the slide (vertical band ~5-15% height), between the outer frame and the content box, in large bold red (#CC0000) sans-serif type.
5. Top-right corner of the slide, outside the content box: draw a circle filled yellow (#FFFACD) with a dark indigo (#4B0082) outline, containing the number '17' in dark text.
6. Inside the content box, left column (x ~10-55%, y ~20-65%): place the bold black (#000000) header 'Questions:-' at the top of the column.

10. Right side of the content box (x ~55-90%, y ~20-60%): build a 2x2 grid of four small, equal-sized charts, each with black (#000000) axes, small tick marks, and no numeric axis labels.
11. In all four charts plot the same blue (#0000FF) scatter data dots and the same light green (#90EE90) smooth underlying curve (dot count and exact curve shape are not specified in the source).
12. 13. Add a small text label to each chart: 'M = 0' on the top-left plot, 'M = 1' on the top-right plot, 'M = 3' on the bottom-left plot, 'M = 9' on the bottom-right plot (all four values carry the source's [?] uncertainty marker); place each label at the top-right inside its plot (in-plot placement assumed, not specified in source).
14. Do not recreate the pen/mouse cursor icon shown near 'generalize' in the video frame: per animation_state it is a live lecture-annotation artifact, not slide content.
